Taking their worldly possessions, around 3,000 of them made it to Morocco, moving port-to-port in search of a new home until they settled in the ruins of the fortress at Rabat. Thousands of other Morisco refugees, mostly from Andalusia, would follow in the coming years, building a new walled town outside the existing fortress. Following the Moriscos’ arrival, others from further north began to make their way to Rabat-Salé. They arrived due to the end of Spain’s wars with England and the Netherlands, which left thousands of sailors unemployed.
